subject: fuaran-core-compute
$comment: What the proof leg COSTS, declared per module, so that a growth in prover time is named rather than discovered when CI times out. Adopted from the proof-leg kit's templates/modules.json (Phase 259); the three entries, the seeding rules and the contention threshold are carried from the Fuaran.Core repository's own file, where these three models were first checked and measured on the same prover pin — re-seed them from this repository's own runs as they accumulate, by the rules below. `proofs/check.ps1` (through `proofs/kit/check-proof-leg.ps1`) reads this file: every green CHECK line prints the module's measured seconds beside its budget, and a run over budget prints a named COST warning, never a failure; a run under an entry's `floorSeconds` FAILS the leg, because a module that verified faster than it can is evidence of a warm cache rather than of speed. `packages` names the packages a model covers; `proofs/coverage-exclusions.json` records every packable package no model names, and the `Proofs.Coverage` family holds the two to the roster both ways.

seeding.rule: budgetSeconds = max(2 x the slowest observed cold-cache run, minimumBudgetSeconds), rounded up to the next 10s.
seeding.$comment: The tolerance is applied ONCE, here, when a number is seeded — `check.ps1` multiplies nothing, so the pair it prints is the measurement against the ceiling and there is no second arithmetic to hold in your head. Seeded from the SLOWEST observed cold run rather than the median, deliberately: on the machine these were measured on, six concurrent sessions inflate a cold check by ~1.8x with nothing about the tree changed (TreeOps 45s to 77s, JsonParse 52s to 99s within one three-run leg), so a budget seeded from the median would fire on a busy afternoon and teach a reader to ignore it. The 20s minimum is for the sub-5s modules, where 2x is inside ordinary process-start noise. These are figures from a Windows dev machine; CI's windows-latest runner is a different machine and its first runs are what will say whether the tolerance is generous enough there. If it is not, that is a bump, and a bump is recorded.
seeding.$namingNote: RENAMED by Phase 155, from `floorSeconds`. That was the same word the per-entry time floor uses for the opposite thing — this one is the smallest a BUDGET may be (a floor under the CEILING), an entry's `floorSeconds` is the smallest a RUN may be, and the `Skeleton` entry below had to spend two sentences telling the two apart. Renamed rather than documented, because Phase 155 ships this file's skeleton in `proofs/kit/templates/modules.json` and a skeleton that carries a collision ships it to everyone who copies it. Nothing reads this key but people: `check.ps1` reads only the `modules` array, so the rename moved four prose readers and no code.

floorSeeding.rule: floorSeconds = the FASTEST genuine cold run ever observed, halved, rounded DOWN to the whole second; 0 for a module whose fastest genuine cold run is under 5s.
floorSeeding.$comment: The floor is the budget's mirror and the two are deliberately NOT symmetric in what they do. A budget is a ceiling and a smoke detector: an overshoot is a true measurement of a true cost, so it warns and the leg stays green. A floor is a gate: `check.ps1` FAILS the leg on the spot, naming the module and the time, because a module that verified faster than it can possibly verify has not told you it is fast — it has told you the measurement is worthless, and everything measured after it shares the apparatus. Implausibly fast is the one direction in which a lie looks like good news. WHAT BOUGHT THIS (2026-09-14, recorded in Phase 143's outcome): an orphaned background `check.ps1` kept writing the then-shared `proofs/obj/cache` while a replacement run started in the same worktree; the replacement found the orphan's `.checked` files, reported `TreeOps 0s`, `Skeleton 0s`, `Chain 0s` and printed `==== proofs: green`. It was caught by a human reading the timings. Phase 164 closed the cause (a per-invocation cache directory, `obj/cache-<pid>`) and this file closes the class (a floor, so a shared cache anywhere else still cannot pass as evidence). Seeded from the FASTEST observed rather than the median, and halved on top, for the mirror of the budget's reason: a floor that fires on a fast quiet machine teaches a reader to ignore it, and the failure this catches lands at or near ZERO seconds, so an enormous margin costs nothing in detection. The 5s rule is for the modules where halving lands inside process-start noise — `Skeleton` checks in about one second, and any positive floor there would be a coin toss. An ABSENT `floorSeconds` is a cost finding rather than a failure (a sibling adding a model should no more go red for a floor nobody has measured than for a budget nobody has measured); an explicit 0 is a different statement and reads as one. `check.ps1 -NoFloor` is the deliberate opt-out for a machine genuinely that fast, and it says so in the log. Re-seeding a floor DOWNWARDS is the same recorded act as bumping a budget upwards: the new number, the `fastestSeconds` it came from, and your phase. One asymmetry makes that act rarer than the budget's: a run FASTER than the recorded `fastestSeconds` but still above the floor leaves the floor correct and merely conservative, so it obliges nothing — where a run over budget is a live finding every time. Only a breach forces the number, and a breach is first a reason to look for a second writer. The figures here were seeded on 2026-09-14 from the fastest of three cold passes on one quiet Windows dev machine; CI's runner is a different machine, and if it is genuinely faster than half of these, that is a re-seed and a re-seed is recorded.

contentionSeeding.rule: threshold = a number above the median ratio of a measured QUIET pass on the SLOWEST machine that runs this leg, and at or below the median ratio of the contention worth naming. Place it high: a false label suppresses a real regression, where a missed label costs only what the leg did before.
contentionSeeding.$comment: SINCE PHASE 171 the leg reports, at the end of every run, the MEDIAN over the modules the working tree did NOT change of that module's measured seconds divided by the `measuredSeconds` its entry below records — the run's CONTENTION FACTOR. Above this threshold every cost finding from that run is LABELLED a contended pass where the closing verdict prints it, and a labelled finding is explicitly NOT a re-seed obligation: re-seeding a budget from a contended run raises a ceiling to fit a slow afternoon, which is exactly how a budget stops meaning anything. `check.ps1 -Strict` promotes only the UNLABELLED findings. Nothing is multiplied into a measurement — the seconds a green line prints stay the wall clock, and the factor sits beside them. THE SCALE IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE AND WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (Phase 171): `measuredSeconds` is not a typical cost, it is by `seeding`'s own rule the SLOWEST cold run ever observed for that module, and most of the entries below were seeded under six concurrent sessions — so the ratio's neutral point sits well BELOW one. A quiet cold pass of the whole leg on this dev machine measured x0.29 over sixteen contributing modules (DagFold 14s, WireDecode 9s, TreeOps 19s, Chain 4s, JsonParse 19s, Preservation 13s, TreeDiff 4s, WireCanon 9s, Vocabulary 3s, VocabularyProofs 5s, DocVocabulary 4s, DocVocabularyProofs 7s, ScoreVocabulary 7s, ScoreVocabularyProofs 14s, ColumnOps 12s, Capability 6s; machine idle, nothing else on it), and the SAME leg under four sustained competing provers measured x0.40 (every large module 1.4-1.7x its quiet time). The three incidents this threshold exists to name — Chain's 35s/31s against 30s, Phase 162's TreeOps at 145s, Phase 182's Capability at 75s against 20s — all ran beside six concurrent SESSIONS, which is the load `measuredSeconds` itself was seeded under, so they sit near x1.0 by construction. 0.8 is therefore placed between: 2.7x above this machine's quiet pass, so a machine up to 2.7x slower still reads an ordinary pass as ordinary, and below the x1.0 the recorded incidents produce. WHAT THAT COSTS, said plainly: four bare competing provers on this machine (x0.40) is NOT labelled, so the threshold does not fire on mild contention — deliberate, because a false label is the expensive error and a missed one leaves the reader exactly where Phase 148 left them. THE OPEN QUESTION is the same one `seeding` records for its own tolerance: the baseline is machine-dependent, CI's windows-latest runner is a different and slower machine, and its first runs are what will say whether 0.8 clears ITS quiet pass. If it does not, that is a re-seed and a re-seed is recorded — the new number, the quiet factor it came from, and the phase. `minimumSamples` is the smallest set the median may be taken over; below it the leg reports the factor as not computed rather than taking a median of one. The per-module cut — a module whose `measuredSeconds` is under `floorSeeding.zeroBelowSeconds` does not vote, because at whole-second resolution 0s against a recorded 2s is a ratio of 0 and says nothing about the machine — is that rule's number reused rather than a second one minted here; it excludes Skeleton, Limits and WireVersioning. Each entry below may also carry an optional `contentionFactor` beside its `measuredSeconds`, recorded by whichever phase next seeds that number: it says what the machine was doing when the measurement was taken, so a later reader can tell a budget seeded quiet from one seeded busy. It is PROVENANCE ONLY — `check.ps1` holds it to its shape and computes nothing from it, for the same reason the factor is never multiplied into a measurement — and an absent one reads as `not recorded`, never as 1. No entry below carries one yet: this phase re-seeds no budget, and back-filling a figure for a pass nobody measured would be inventing the very provenance the field exists to carry.

modules.note: The WIRE_FORMAT section-21 resource limits as named premises. Eight constants and two lemmas about the relations between them, so there is nothing here for the prover to work at: both cold runs measured under a second and the entry sits at the 20s floor for exactly the reason the seeding note gives — 2x of a 1s measurement is inside process-start noise, and a budget that fires on a busy afternoon teaches a reader to ignore it. If this one ever overshoots, the module has stopped being a table of constants and the growth is the finding. Its floorSeconds is 0 by the floorSeeding rule's zeroBelowSeconds clause, for Skeleton's reason and more so: the fastest cold run measured was under a second, so half of it is inside process-start noise and any positive floor here would be a coin toss. Like Skeleton's, this 0 is honest about covering nothing — what covers this module against a warm cache is the per-invocation cache directory Phase 164 put in check.ps1, not this number. Copied into this repository because Pipeline opens it; it covers no package here (its constants describe the wire format, which the substrate produces).

The compute strand's op algebra — `ColumnOps.apply` / `canApply` / `invert` / `Diff.toOps` clause for clause, the five Preservation clauses proved for columns, and `Diff.toOps`'s reconstruction. Self-contained (opens nothing) and cheap: default context, no scoped options, the whole module discharges at the leg's own rlimit of 40 under `--quake 3`. SEEDED BY PHASE 176: three cold runs through the kit on this machine, 47s, 31s, 22s (the first carrying the prover's first-run cost, beside concurrent sessions), and the prover invoked directly on the same file with the same flags during authoring, fresh verification each time, 9-20s — so the budget is 2x the slowest kit run rounded up to the next 10s (100s) and the floor is half the fastest genuine run rounded down (4s from 9s), per the two rules above. The two proof shapes that cost anything are the well-formedness preservation for `AppendRows` (a forall over the columns, threaded through `typed_append_aux`) and the diff's two walks (`changed_apply`, `inserts_apply`), each an induction carrying an invariant about the prefix already processed.

The counted pipeline driver AND its expression evaluator — `Fuaran.Core.DataFrame`'s closed `ColExpr` and `Transform` algebra with every payload type and `EvalError`, the private `evalExpr` with its four inner loops, `evalFilter`, `evalDerive`, `evalStep`'s dispatch, `evalPipelineWithInEnvCounted`'s `costOf` and `go` clause for clause, and `evalPipelineWithInEnv` as the projection, over two parameters (the cell primitives, the twelve verbs that evaluate no expression); `eval_total`, `budget_monotone`, `visits_le_nodes`, `rows_visits_le`, `work_bounded` (the §21.8 limit as a hypothesis, the work read off the concrete evaluator), `over_limit_not_refused` (the finding) and `uncounted_is_projection` proved. Opens `Limits` for the one constant, default context, no scoped options, no SMT pattern, every type parameter `Type0`: the whole module discharges at the leg's own rlimit of 40 under `--quake 3` with no query needing more than one attempt, and Phase 234's port verified on the FIRST prover run as Phase 154's driver had — the proofs are six structural inductions over the pipeline list, three mutual inductions over the expression (`eval_expr` and its four loops, `expr_visits` and its four, `visits_le_nodes` and its four), the well-formedness lemmas under `eval_derive`, and the arithmetic is the three `FStar.Math.Lemmas` calls that carry a multiplication through a sum. RE-SEEDED BY PHASE 234 (Phase 154's 5s/6s driver-only entry is superseded — the evaluator is the cost) from three cold runs of the prover invoked directly on the file with the leg's own flags against a cache holding only `Limits` — 17.3s, 17.0s, 16.9s — so by `seeding`'s rule the budget is 40s (2x17.3 is 34.6, rounded up to the next 10) and by `floorSeeding`'s the floor is half the fastest genuine cold run rounded down (8s from 16.9s). The phase's own `check.ps1 -Runs 3` leg reading is recorded on the README's theorem 14 cost section beside the contention label the kit gave it. A quiet machine will run it faster; per `floorSeeding` that leaves the floor correct and merely conservative unless a run lands under 8s, which is first a reason to look for a second writer. If this entry ever overshoots, look first at `expr_visits` and `visits_le_nodes`: each arm re-evaluates the sub-expression to follow the short circuit, so a constructor added to `ColExpr` widens three mutual walks at once, and the evaluator's arm for it is where the cost lands. RE-SEEDED BY PHASE 269, which added sections 11 and 12 — the planner's reorder theorem (`eval_extends`, a mutual induction over the expression and its four loops proving an expression answers the same on two rows that agree on what it reads; `filter_ext`; `derive_then_filter` per extension shape, at fuel 4 and an rlimit of 120 in a scoped option, the one place the file departs from the default context) and the totality verdict's soundness (`verdict_sound`, a second mutual induction over the same five walks, threading the typer and the `admits` record) — roughly doubling the module's proof text. Three cold runs of the leg on this machine beside a concurrent sibling's build and gate: 125s, 125s, 89s (`--quake 3`), against the 17s Phase 234 seeded, so by `seeding`'s rule the budget is 2x the slowest rounded up to the next 10s (250s). The floor and `fastestSeconds` are Phase 234's: this phase's fastest run was slower than the recorded fastest, which per `floorSeeding` obliges nothing. If this entry overshoots again, look first at the two mutual inductions — each arm of `eval_expr` is walked by both — and at `derive_then_filter_replace`, the one lemma that needed the scoped rlimit.
